title: Every Spark Root Edit must pass Spark Risk Council review before a vote can be triggered
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.2 requires that "all Spark Root Edit proposals must be reviewed by the Spark Risk Council," and A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 makes the outcome binding: the Facilitator triggers the token holder poll only "where the proposal passes review by the SRC (defined as 'Passed SRC Review')."

The distinction between advisory and gating review is what matters. An advisory council publishes an opinion that voters may ignore; a gating council determines whether the vote happens. Spark's Risk Council is the second kind, which makes it a genuine branch of the Agent's governance rather than a research function.

The justification is asymmetry of expertise. Spark's Artifact governs collateral deployment, lending parameters and cross-chain liquidity, where a change can be popular and still solvency-threatening, and where the harm may not be visible to a general electorate until it materializes.

The structural cost is that two unelected gates — SRC risk review and Facilitator alignment review — sit between a proposal and the electorate. Spark's governance is therefore better described as expert-screened token voting than as token holder control.
description: Expert risk review is a mandatory precondition, not advice: the Facilitator only calls the poll once the proposal is recorded as 'Passed SRC Review'.
